newsitem.title: BRAZIL: GE unit bows out of Brazil's Credireal sale.
newsitem.headline: GE unit bows out of Brazil's Credireal sale.

text.p: General Electric Co's General Electric Capital Corp will not participate in Thursday's privatization auction of Minas Gerais state bank Credireal, a top company official said on Tuesday.
"The company is out of the auction Thursday," said Nahid Chicani, a GE vice president in Brazil. He said GE might have lost interest in Credireal because of the sale's conditions.
Credireal, formally known as Banco de Credito Real de Minas Gerais SA, is to be sold for a base price of 121.3 million reais. It is the second Brazilian state bank due to be privatized.

Cia de Investimentos Latinoamericana is a company created by Brazil's Banco Pactual to seek investment opportunities in the country's banking sector. Tabal Participacoes and Varejo are units of Bozano Simonsen group, which owns investment bank Banco Bozano, Simonsen.
Prequalified investors interested in bidding for Credireal are required to sign up for the auction on Tuesday.

Pactual President Luiz Cesar Fernandes declined to say whether the company, which so far represents a foreign bank in the Credireal sale, will bid Thursday. But he said there was investor interest in Credireal was not strong.
